newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rights commission releases riot report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rights commission releases riot report.

text.p: Indonesia's official human rights watchdog said on Saturday that five people were killed, 149 people injured and 23 still missing as a result of the July riots that rocked Jakarta.

"The authorities must continue to look for those who are missing," Bachruddin Lopa, secteray-general of the National Commission on Human Rights, told reporters while releasing a final report on the July 27 violence.
An earlier preliminary report by the commission had caught the government off balance by saying five people had died and 74 were missing.

The government had given a figure of four dead and none missing in the riots, the worst violence in the capital in more than two decades in which a number of buildings were also burned in one area of the city of 10 million.
"The government wants the rights commission to prove the figures with acceptable evidence," State Secretary Murdiono said at the time.
The riots were sparked by a police assault on the Jakarta headquarters of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
The police moved in to evict supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri, who was ousted as the PDI leader by a government-backed faction of the party in June.
The human rights commission was set up by the government in 1993. It has won a reputation for integrity and a willingness to criticise the country's powerful military establishment.
